newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace activists hold out on BP oil platform.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace activists hold out on BP oil platform.

text.p: Greenpeace activists chained to a mobile oil platform in the Atlantic were determined to stay on after boarding the British Petroleum rig two days ago, Greenpeace said on Monday.
Two activists were currently on the Stena Dee platform of the original seven who climbed the rig on Saturday to protest against development of the Foinaven oilfield north-west of Scotland.

A Greenpeace spokeswoman said the oil rig was 50 miles north-west of the Orkney islands and 22 miles south of the Foinaven field, the first of BP's Atlantic Frontier drilling operations due to produce oil.
Weather conditions had improved with a strong breeze blowing on Monday morning after very strong winds and three meter high waves overnight.
"Safety-wise they're fine," a Greenpeace spokeswoman said, adding no efforts were being made to get the campaigners off the Stena Dee platform.
The two German activists -- one male, one female -- have been chained on one of the Stena Dee's legs since midday on Sunday, BP said.
A BP spokesman said the company's priority at the moment was the safety of all on board the rig which was heading from Norway to work on Foinaven.
Greenpeace wants the Stena Dee to return to Norway and called on BP to abandon the Foinaven project, the first to be developed in deep waters west of the Shetland Islands.
"Protecting the climate is not an optional extra, it is an absolute necessity. We're here for the duration," campaigner Liz Pratt on board of a Greenpeace vessel said in a statement.
The BP spokesman said Greenpeace's action would not delay its overall operations at the much-delayed Foinaven which is now expected to produce oil by the end of the year.
The project has suffered a series of technological mishaps. It was originally due onstream the middle of 1996.
